title: PRD: Trigger matrix and safe-degradation paths for Optimize eval alarms
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a deterministic trigger matrix, tiered regression thresholds, and safe-degradation (rollback) paths for Redwood Optimize evaluations. The intent is to make A/B and canary rollouts for model/quantization/parameter changes auditable and automatable with clear decision boundaries so Platform and Customer-facing traffic do not experience unbounded quality regressions.

Background and motivation:
Optimize is being used to recommend batching/quantization/model variants. Teams have run into ambiguous degradation signals during rollouts: single-signal blips, cohort-specific regressions, and noisy metrics that lead to either premature rollbacks or late interventions. We need a standardized, actionable trigger matrix that: (a) distinguishes statistical noise from meaningful regressions, (b) prescribes immediate automated actions for high-severity regressions, and (c) provides human-in-the-loop escalation for gray-area signals.

Scope (in):
- Define primary and secondary evaluation metrics (weighted quality score, per-cohort loss, latency P95, hallucination rate proxy).
- Stratified prompt set sampling plan across 6 cohorts (webchat, search, creative, summarization, code, compliance-sensitive).
- Statistical testing family (two-sided bootstrap + Bernoulli tests for binary safety flags).
- Canary and A/B traffic sizing, rollout windows, and automatic decision rules.
- Playbook of automated actions mapped to trigger tiers (auto-fallback, pause, rollback, open incident).

Out of scope:
- New metric instrumentation systems (we rely on existing runtime dashboards and metric pipelines).
- Long-term ML model retraining strategies.

Assumptions:
- Baseline golden promptset and historical distributions are available in Optimize evals.
- Dashboards expose per-route and per-cohort time series with 1-minute granularity.

Risks and mitigations:
- Small-sample cohorts may produce high-variance signals -> mitigation: require minimum sample sizes or longer evaluation windows and use Bayesian shrinkage priors when computing cohort deltas.
- Multiple comparisons across cohorts -> mitigation: apply FDR correction for multi-cohort hypothesis tests and require cross-cohort confirmation for automatic rollback unless severity is high.

Stakeholders:
- Runtime / Serving Eng: implement hooks for traffic shaping and rollback automation.
- Applied ML / Optimize team: define weighted quality scoring and promptset composition.
- Console / Observability: expose signals and runbooks in the rollout UI.
- Customer Success and Trust: notification templates for impacted customers.
acceptance_criteria: Primary metric defined: Weighted Quality Score (WQS) combining human-rated quality, hallucination flag rate, and latency penalty. Formula and weights documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/optimize/wqs-spec
A/B test rule: a candidate variant passes if WQS delta >= -0.75% (non-inferiority margin) with 95% bootstrap CI and p >= 0.95 in favor of control OR shows positive improvement > 0.5% with p >= 0.95.
Canary sizing: initial canary serves 3% of traffic for 2 hours with continuous monitoring; extended canary to 10% for 24 hours if no Tier-1 signals occur.

Regression tier definitions implemented: Tier 1 (Severe): WQS drop >= 3.0% OR hallucination-rate increase >= 50% relative to baseline across global traffic; triggers immediate automated rollback. Tier 2 (Moderate): WQS drop 1.0%–3.0% OR cohort-specific drop >= 2.0%; triggers automated pause + alert for 30-minute human review. Tier 3 (Minor): WQS drop 0.5%–1.0% OR noisy signal; triggers enhanced sampling and 48-hour watch window.

Statistical tests in pipeline: two-sided bootstrap for WQS deltas (n>=200 samples per cohort) and Bernoulli test for binary safety flags; code in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-evals/pull/512

Multi-signal requirement for automatic rollback: automatic rollback requires at least one Tier-1 global signal OR two independent Tier-2 signals across separate cohorts unless manual override by on-call SRE.
Minimum sample sizes enforced automatically: no auto-decisions for cohorts with fewer than 200 promptset samples in the evaluation window; such cohorts are flagged for manual review.
Console integrations: rollout UI shows live WQS delta, per-cohort breakdown, p-values, and recommended action buttons (Auto-rollback, Pause, Extend Canary).
Runbook present and linked in console with on-call steps, notification templates, postmortem checklist, and owner assignments.
implementation_notes: Telemetry: emit WQS components at token-level and aggregate in 1m and 5m windows; add tags for cohort, route, model-variant and quantization-profile.
Automation: implement a stateless decision engine that subscribes to metrics, computes bootstrap CIs every minute, and publishes actions to the rollout controller.
Safety overrides: on-call SRE can force 'freeze' to prevent further automated rollbacks for specific customers via Console toggle.
Data retention: store evaluation windows and raw prompt samples for 90 days to support regressions audits and A/B reproducibility.
Front-end: show clear color-coded signal states (green/amber/red) and a short text rationale for each recommended action.
Backwards compatibility: decision engine must support legacy Optimize metric names for a 3-month migration window.
